findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is an empty subclass of an ABC with unimplemented abstract methods, so constructing it raises TypeError
findings.description:
The diff replaces the concrete `evaluate()` in `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` with `pass`, while changing its base from `DetectorHandler` to `StatefulDetectorHandler`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members that this class does not implement: `counter_names` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:144), `get_dedupe_value` (:151), `get_group_key_values` (:159), and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (:167, added by this diff). Python's ABC machinery therefore refuses to instantiate the class.

The failure path: `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`. `process_detectors` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:53) calls that property on every detector it is given, so such a detector would raise inside the detector loop. Before this diff, the class defined `evaluate()` on `DetectorHandler`, which was its only abstract member, so it instantiated and returned `[]`.

Why this is a CONCERN and not a FAIL: `metric_alert_fire` / `MetricAlertFire` appears only in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py, and nothing in the repo creates a `Detector` with that type, so the crash is latent in this tree. No test references `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, so the suite will not catch it. Once any code creates a detector of this type, this becomes a FAIL. The fix is either to implement the four abstract members or to keep the placeholder on `DetectorHandler` and return `{}` until the stateful handler exists.
